text:
Ryan Shea left Pittsburgh for Edmonton and is now playing almost 23 minutes a night. With Darnell Nurse gone to San Jose, the Oilers have handed him a top-four job, and Oilers Nation has already run the comparison between the two. He has one goal and seven points in 25 games, blocks a lot of shots (38) and kills penalties.

Last season is why the Oilers took the chance. Evolving-Hockey had him worth 3.3 wins above replacement in Pittsburgh, fifth among 215 defensemen, mostly from even-strength offense. Their own note adds the warning: his results ran well ahead of his chances (1.9 expected wins), so some of that was hot shooting and goaltending around him.

This season looks more like the expected version. His on-ice numbers at five on five are fine relative to his teammates (the Oilers do 4.5 points better in expected goal share with him on), but the points have dried up: two assists in his last ten games, both in the last week. Our range has him finishing around 32 points. The question isn't whether he can hold the minutes. It's whether the offense that made last season special was ever really his.
